title: Task-conditional data re-upload schedule Mirror
amendment_01: Initial development seed 101701 produced only three unique task sign-label functions, with two duplicate task functions. Development-only seed selection fixed seed 101702, which yields four distinct task functions; selection used only task uniqueness, not Mirror-control outcome. Fresh seeds/gates remain unchanged.
hypothesis: A scalar task phase on each repeated input-upload rotation can preserve task accuracy with less actual storage than an independent VQC bank, beyond the ordinary scalar-angle control.
mirror_coordinate: one task phase added to both qubit input rotation angles at each re-upload block
logical_multiplicity: four task-specific classification functions on one fixed gate skeleton

development.selection_metric: four unique task label functions, teacher agreement, sampled accuracy, actual payload bytes, logical gate schedule

storage.format: UTF-8 JSON header plus contiguous little-endian float32 arrays

success_gate: Mirror retains >=98% of independent teacher shot accuracy, saves >=25% actual bytes vs independent bank, and beats ordinary scalar schedule control by >=2 percentage points with equal shots and gates.
failure_gate: Mirror aliases native scalar schedule, or misses the quality/storage gate.
boundaries: ideal statevector plus binomial measurement sampling
